The requirements stem from President Donald Trump’s “One Big Beautiful Bill Act,” which Wisconsin and other states must implement.

sources.title: Nvidia's one-man board: How Trump inherited Jensen Huang's scandal
sources.description: A euphoric Wall Street erupted Monday as President Trump personally secured Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, trading on the end of a scandal that — in reality — has only just begun. Why it matters: By assuring Nvidia's board that Huang poses no national security risk, Trump has staked the credibility of the U.S. government on a CEO who lied about his relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.

headlines.name: Iowa
headlines.headline: Federal Court Clears Way for Iowa Lead Ammunition Detonation
headlines.description: The U.S. Army is moving forward with a controversial plan to detonate nearly five tons of hazardous bomb-making chemicals at an ammunition plant in Iowa after a federal court ruled cleared the way late Monday. The blast, which is set for Wednesday, is prompting fears from residents that it will trigger a toxic cloud of dust. NBC’s Shaquille Brewster reports for TODAY.

headlines.name: Megaspeed
headlines.headline: Commerce adds Megaspeed to trade blacklist
headlines.description: The Trump administration on Monday added the company at the heart of the Nvidia scandal, Megaspeed, to a trade blacklist designed to prevent it from obtaining US-made semiconductors. The Singapore-based company was added to the Commerce Department’s entity list on Monday afternoon, plans that were first reported by Semafor.
